journeys.title: The Mosel, Trier to Koblenz
journeys.text: Meander after meander cut into Devonian slate, where Europe's steepest vineyards lean south over the water: the amphitheatre of Piesport, the Doctor above Bernkastel, Wehlen's sundial, Erden's red-slate Prälat and the walled terraces of the Terrassenmosel before Koblenz.

sites.name: Neumagener Weinschiff
sites.cls: Roman funerary monument, c. 220 AD (replica on site)

sites.name: Winninger Uhlen
sites.cls: Einzellage; three sections are EU PDOs since 2018

journeys.title: The Douro, Barca d'Alva to Porto
journeys.text: Downstream from the dry schist of the Douro Superior, through the Pinhão terraces of the Cima Corgo and the greener Baixo Corgo, to the lodges of Vila Nova de Gaia, where Port rests in casks across the river from Porto.

sites.name: Quinta do Vale Meão
sites.cls: Birthplace of Barca Velha; Douro Boys estate

sites.name: Quinta da Foz
sites.cls: Cálem's quinta at the mouth of the Pinhão

sites.name: Miradouro de São Leonardo de Galafura

journeys.title: The Rhône, Vienne to Avignon
journeys.text: Granite first: Côte-Rôtie and Condrieu on the right bank, then the Hermitage hill above Tain. South of Valence the valley opens, the mistral takes over, and the river runs past Lirac and Tavel to the galets of Châteauneuf-du-Pape.

journeys.title: The Loire, Sancerre to Nantes
journeys.text: Flint and chalk around Sancerre and Pouilly, the tuffeau caves of Vouvray and Montlouis, Chinon and Bourgueil on the Vienne's edge, the schist of Savennières and the Layon, then the Muscadet country on the last stretch to the Atlantic.

sites.name: Clos de la Coulée de Serrant

journeys.title: The Rhine through the Rheingau
journeys.text: For 30 km the Rhine flows west, so the Rheingau's slopes face south over a broad river that reflects the sun and softens frost: Eltville, Erbach, Johannisberg and Rüdesheim, until the river turns north into the gorge at Lorch.

sites.name: Schloss Johannisberg
sites.cls: Historic estate; Ortsteil site needing no village name

journeys.title: The Danube through the Wachau
journeys.text: Melk to Krems through a narrow cut in the Bohemian Massif: dry-stone terraces of gneiss and loess at Spitz, Weissenkirchen, Dürnstein and Loiben, home of Smaragd Grüner Veltliner and Riesling, with the Kremstal waiting at the valley mouth.

journeys.title: Garonne and Gironde, Langon to Saint-Estèphe
journeys.text: Past the cold Ciron that brings autumn mists to Barsac and Sauternes, down through Bordeaux, then along the Gironde estuary where the gravel croupes of Margaux, Saint-Julien, Pauillac and Saint-Estèphe look out over the water.

sites.name: Musée du Vin et du Négoce, Chartrons

journeys.title: The Dordogne, Castillon to Bourg
journeys.text: The right bank: Castillon's slopes, the limestone plateau and clay of Saint-Émilion, Pomerol's iron-rich gravel behind Libourne, the hills of Fronsac, and the Côtes de Bourg where the Dordogne meets the Garonne.

sites.name: Battle of Castillon Monument
sites.cls: Site of the battle of 17 July 1453

journeys.title: The Napa Valley floor, Calistoga to Napa
journeys.text: Down the valley from volcanic Calistoga to the fog-cooled south: St. Helena, the Rutherford bench, Oakville and Yountville, then Oak Knoll and the town of Napa, with the Mayacamas to the west and the Vaca range to the east.

stops.name: Oak Knoll District of Napa Valley
